page.layout: Running head across the top of the text block: "Lib. II." and "Scutum Regium." on one line. One text column, full width, with a narrow right margin holding three notes (p, q, r) beside the text. Page number 103 at top right, above the margin. Signature "H 4" and catchword "Sed" at the foot of the column.

main_text.p: p Tom.2. pag.546.nalibus ita scribit {p}P Cæsar Baronius [Sic exconsuetis titulis Dionysius dicit Imperatores illos sanctissimos viros, quà & Paulus Ἀποστολος[?] scelestissimum hominem Fœlicem alloquens ait; Optime Fœlix: cùm alioquin, etiam ex proprietate quoque vocis Imperatores, licet nefandissimos, tamen sanctissimos appellare potuissent: nam Cicero ait; quare suo iure noster ille Ennius sanctos appellat Poetas, quod quasi Deorum dono atque munere, nobis commendati esse videantur. Si igitur quod à Deo datum creditur, sanctum dicitur; cùm constet ex Christianæ Legis prescripto, Principes etiam malos à Deo dari in ultionem peccatorum (secundum illud, {q}Dabo vobis regem in furore meo,& {r}qui regnare facit hominem hypocritam:) hac quidem ratione utique potuit illos nominare sanctissimos. Hastenus Baronius.] Quod igitur ipse Deus sanctum fecit homo ne violet, & quæ Deus coniunxit, imperium scilicet & Imperatorem, homo ne separet, quod aliquando tamen iustè & legitimè fieri posse, tuipse (ut in sequentibus apparebit) obnixè Baroni cotedis. Sed

page.notes: Margin notes: "p Tom.2. pag.546." at top right; "q Osee 13." (printed "Ofee 13"[?]) and "r Iob.27." beside the text at the marks {q} and {r}. The mark {p} in the text is taken as the letter preceding "Cæsar Baronius"[?]. The first Greek word "Ἀποστολος" is badly printed and uncertain; the printed form appears to mix Greek and Latin letters. "Hastenus" is printed with a long-s form and may be "Hactenus"[?]. The word "nalibus" at the start is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The brackets "[Sic" and "Baronius.]" are as printed.
